name: BYTE PHANTOM
realCapabilities: Network Shutdown Intelligence: cross-platform route/DNS/upstream/endpoint isolation using three independent system DNS names and four HTTPS providers
Per-destination reachability matrix identifies partial connectivity and endpoint-specific failures instead of treating one reachable test host as proof of full internet access
OUTAGE WATCH stores successful DNS and HTTPS target counts for each sample and exports the counts to CSV/JSON
OUTAGE WATCH issue confirmation: two consecutive qualifying failures before opening an incident and two consecutive successful HTTPS checks before recovery
OUTAGE WATCH DNS, HTTPS, and gateway response latency history with a recent trend view and rolling median baselines
Cross-platform OUTAGE WATCH: interval-based gateway/DNS/HTTPS connectivity checks, local incident start/recovery timeline, and JSON/CSV export
Cross-platform private IPv4 Network Radar and persistent local journal
Interactive observed LAN map
Read-only gateway, DNS resolver, transport, interface, local IPv4, and default-route intelligence on Windows and Android
Layered connectivity diagnosis: active route snapshot, one local gateway ICMP echo, system DNS resolution, and two independent HTTPS/TLS checks on Windows and Android
DNS resolver intelligence: direct UDP/53 DNS A-query tests for configured IPv4 DNS servers and Cloudflare, Google Public DNS, and Quad9 reference resolvers
DNS answer comparison for example.com and iana.org across configured IPv4 DNS servers and Cloudflare, Google Public DNS, and Quad9
Non-public DNS answer review flags and peer-majority divergence indicators, with explicit CDN/GeoDNS caveats
Fastest resolver recommendation based on average latency across successful answers for both query names
Local DNS test history retaining the latest 20 test summaries for up to 30 days; manual copy of resolver IP without changing system settings
Repeated DNS resolver stability sampling: three direct DNS A-query samples for each of example.com and iana.org per configured IPv4 resolver and public reference
Per-name answer consistency, sample response rate, median latency, latency range and median absolute deviation jitter metrics
Cross-resolver comparison now uses only repeat-stable answer sets; unstable repeat answers are explicitly marked inconclusive
DNS resolver recommendations require repeat-stable answers for both query names and are ranked by median latency across the stable names
Local history captures sample success rate, number of repeat-stable resolvers, best resolver median latency and jitter; visual trend covers latest eight tests
DNS failover candidate selector populated only by repeat-stable IPv4 resolvers from the latest three-round DNS stability test
Windows DNS apply on the active default-route adapter after explicit in-app confirmation and native UAC Administrator approval
Local backup of the original Windows DNS mode (automatic/DHCP or static) and original IPv4 DNS server list before applying an override
Post-apply verification of the selected Windows DNS server, with an explicit restore operation and a second confirmation if current DNS differs from the app-applied setting
Android DNS state display and launch of Android wireless/network settings for a manual DNS configuration; no privileged device-wide setting changes or VPN tunnel

android.nativeBridge: Capacitor 6 Java plugin with bundled capacitor.js JavaScript runtime
android.diagnostics: InetAddress system DNS lookup and HttpURLConnection HTTPS checks

connectivityDiagnostics.gatewayProbe: One ICMP echo request to the active private IPv4 default gateway, when reported and supported
checks: one ICMP echo to the active private IPv4 gateway when reported and supported
system DNS resolution for example.com, iana.org, and cloudflare.com
HTTPS/TLS GET checks against Microsoft, Google, Cloudflare, and Apple test services
connectivityDiagnostics.interpretation: A missing gateway ICMP response is inconclusive because routers or firewalls can filter echo requests. Mixed DNS/HTTPS results indicate partial reachability or target-specific failures. HTTPS success proves reachability to that endpoint only; no test proves unrestricted access to all of the internet.

security: Connectivity diagnostics run only after an explicit user action or while the operator has started OUTAGE WATCH with NETWORK RADAR open. They read the active route, send one ICMP echo to the active private IPv4 gateway when available, perform three system DNS lookups (example.com, iana.org, cloudflare.com), and make four fixed HTTPS GET checks (Microsoft, Google, Cloudflare, Apple). They do not scan LAN hosts or ports, test credentials, exploit devices, or modify network settings. DNS intelligence sends direct DNS A queries only to configured IPv4 DNS servers and fixed public resolver references. DNS answer divergence and non-public address flags are advisory indicators only, not a malware verdict. Resolver recommendations do not change system DNS. Windows DNS changes remain opt-in, limited to the active default-route adapter, require UAC Administrator approval, and preserve a local original-configuration backup. Android opens system network settings for manual changes only.

Added direct DNS-over-UDP resolver tests for configured DNS servers and fixed public resolver references
Added two-name DNS answer comparison, peer-majority divergence review, non-public address flags, recommended resolver copy, and a 20-entry local DNS test history

dnsResolverIntelligence.configuredResolvers: Active interface DNS server list from Windows Get-NetIPConfiguration or Android ConnectivityManager/LinkProperties
dnsResolverIntelligence.comparison: Sorts A-record sets for each name and compares responding resolvers. Flags a resolver only when its answer differs from a clear peer majority; non-public answer ranges are separately flagged for review.
dnsResolverIntelligence.recommendation: Fastest resolver with repeat-stable answers for both example.com and iana.org, ranked by mean of per-name medians. Manual IP copy only.
dnsResolverIntelligence.interpretation: Repeat answer variation can occur with DNS load balancing, CDN/GeoDNS, regional routing, split-horizon policy, or transient conditions. It is not proof of poisoning. Three samples provide an operational consistency indicator, not a statistical guarantee.
dnsResolverIntelligence.stabilityRule: A repeat-stable answer requires at least two matching successful A-record sets out of three for each name.

windows.originalDnsModeDetection: Per-adapter Tcpip interface registry NameServer value distinguishes static DNS from automatic/DHCP DNS; effective DNS server list is backed up as well.
windows.apply: Set-DnsClientServerAddress using the selected repeat-stable IPv4 resolver, then read back the active adapter DNS list and verify the requested server.
windows.restore: Restore automatic DNS using ResetServerAddresses or restore the original static server list. Verify mode/list before deleting the local backup.
windows.conflictHandling: If current DNS no longer matches the last app-applied value, stop and request a second explicit confirmation before overwriting it with the original configuration.
windows.uac: Run elevated PowerShell via the native Windows UAC prompt; cancellation is reported without claiming success.

android.action: Open Android wireless/network settings so the user can manually edit the active network DNS.

limitations: Windows applies IPv4 DNS only to the active default-route adapter; other adapters are not modified.
Android ordinary apps cannot directly change device-wide DNS; the user must apply the selected resolver in system settings.
The original Windows backup is local to the app user-data directory. Keep it until the original configuration is restored or manually recorded.

probes: one ICMP echo to the active private IPv4 gateway when available
three system DNS lookups: example.com, iana.org, cloudflare.com
four fixed HTTPS/TLS checks: Microsoft, Google, Cloudflare, Apple

incidentRules.online: At least one fixed HTTPS endpoint returns a successful status
incidentRules.noDefaultRoute: The active operating system route snapshot reports no IPv4 default route
incidentRules.dnsFailure: System DNS lookup fails while the active gateway answered ICMP
incidentRules.httpsUnreachable: System DNS succeeds but both fixed HTTPS test endpoints fail
incidentRules.indeterminate: Remaining mixed or inconclusive probe results; gateway ICMP silence alone is not considered proof of outage

connectivityWatch.lifecycle: Runs only while NETWORK RADAR is open and the app remains active; closing the panel stops the watch. It is not a background system service.

qualityTrend.rollingBaseline: Median of up to the latest 12 successful measurements per metric

classifications: DNS FAILURE (only when all system DNS checks fail and the gateway answered ICMP)
HTTPS UNREACHABLE (DNS succeeds but all HTTPS providers fail)
PARTIAL CONNECTIVITY (at least one HTTPS provider works but one or more tested names or endpoints fail)
ONLINE (all tested names and HTTPS providers respond)
